Retrieve the original Japanese Primary Prevention Project randomized trial report and supplement: aspirin 100 mg daily versus control in adults aged 60–85, with aligned five-year absolute myocardial-infarction, ischemic-stroke, cardiovascular-death, intracranial-hemorrhage, and major-extracranial-bleeding results, including age and baseline-risk subgroups.

Obtain an age-60-and-over benefit–harm analysis using a common regimen and follow-up horizon, explicitly specifying either a deduplicated first-event endpoint or severity-weighted event burden; report component absolute effects separately and account for overlapping fatal, stroke, and bleeding outcomes.

Independence note: S1, S4, and S9 report the same ASPREE randomized cohort, despite having different source-origin labels. Their overlapping in-trial results must not count as independent corroboration. S2 and S3 also synthesize overlapping primary-prevention trials; compare their included-trial lists before treating pooled treatment-effect estimates as independent.
